001 opens with dust and a library in which Mel and Momiji live. Momiji offers the possibility of finding a rare book; Mel asks whether rarity matters without personal value. The discovered Luna4–21 and Momiji's possession of1–3 become actual shared reading, not a neutral library inventory. Her enthusiastic account combines life, punk, band and film, then presses Mel to read under the Knowledge Liberation Front's equal-knowledge principle. Mel calls this personal desire dressed as collective duty (001u0004–0036).

Mel actually finishes reading and says it is not bad. Her account distinguishes strong characterization and period-sensitive innovation from abrupt troubles, convenient character exits, contradictions, incoherent late plotting and unresolved threads. Momiji partly recognizes earlier criticism while defending memorable characters. Those are represented judgments of a fictional work whose full text is not supplied; neither opinion is an independent critical verdict on Luna. Momiji's demand that Mel have made a masterpiece before criticizing shifts from the work to the critic. The event later revises their interpersonal conduct without establishing that every initial technical objection was false (001u0037–0064;008s002u0016–0019).

The rupture also concerns things outside criticism. Momiji accuses Mel of eating her pancake tempura; Mel admits eating what had been left for a day and suggests labeling it, while Momiji insists that not buying it should suffice. Mel counters with duplicate ordering for a limited edition and a reported two-month collection-application ban. These are competing property and resource claims, not trivial distractions from the plot. Their regret therefore cannot be reduced to one misunderstood review. The printed labels drift notably at001u0015/0031/0058/0070/0075/0078, so content and sequence are kept distinct from any confidently repaired speaker registry. Momiji leaves; Mel's assertion that solitude is easier gives way to an explicit recognition that it is not fine (001u0067–0092).

2. Looking for a final volume produces a different kind of knowledge

Mel first notices Teacher's exhaustion and offers to end the call so Teacher can rest. Teacher's work-avoidance joke, willingness to arrive and attempts to suggest direct apology are represented support with mixed motives, not a limitless adult competence claim. Mel says words are insufficient, then proposes finding Luna22 for Momiji. Her online investigation initially reports a scarce final volume. The three-hour search and failed shop prediction are real local failures, despite her confidence in a perfect calculation (002s001;002s002u0018–0057;s003u0020–0030).

Her account of used books preserves pleasure in browsing, possible treasures, deceptive premium displays and uncertain authenticity. These are Mel's industry formulations, not a verified market survey or legal finding. The explicit hand-holding request is local guidance, not blanket intimacy. Takane's appearance supplies a rival who identifies herself as 三善タカネ, a Publishing Club critic in Red Bear, while claiming to read every local publication. The claim is not audited. Their exchanges retain reciprocal insults, Mel's reported shot near her feet, Takane's formal courtesy, and concern she calls merely toe-level consideration. Their disagreement about creation needing criticism and criticism needing works is not resolved by the narrator declaring a single winner (002s003u0003–0016;003u0016–0027/0039–0059).

Yakumo identifies herself as 荒槇ヤクモ and Publishing Club head, responsible for printing, binding, sales and expansion. Printing both Cherino praise and condemnatory leaflets is her expressed commercial logic: serving both audiences rather than selecting one. Teacher refuses a biography; asking a question does not itself accept Yakumo's proposed bargain, and Mel explicitly challenges that presumption. Teacher later agrees to cooperate for information, while the eventual demand is placed on Mel. Mel refuses strange work, then accepts with a substantive condition: something she can draw and sincerely accepts. Yakumo adds tablet/pen collateral and asks for a signature. Later dialogue says a contract was exchanged, but the exact legal text, validity and enforceability are not inspected (004u0015–0044/0063–0099;014u0012–0016).

The mountain journey includes actual offered heat packs and Mel's memory of Momiji describing an old book as new because it is new to them. That memory changes the earlier preference dispute: knowledge can enrich a recipient without being newly published. It does not erase unequal tastes (005s001u0002–0016).

At the fan event Teacher enjoys action spectacle, separation and artwork; Mel recognizes construction, emotional framing and drawing while questioning each purported ending's continuity. These positive responses retain value even when a work is not the missing original. Their recognition that every booth offers a different fan ending reframes desire as a creative motive. Takane then says the original final volume was never published, revising Mel's online scarcity account. Her account of unfair evaluation and later recognition is her historical explanation, not independently verified publishing history. She also admits deliberately testing how far Mel would go for another person and apologizes to Teacher for the detour (005s002u0014–0057;006u0009–0036).

Takane's concealed fandom becomes explicit: she heads the Luna fan club and wants an ending. Her commitment to respecting multiple interpretations coexists with embarrassment, threatened silencing, particular ambition and later gatekeeping against a newcomer. Equal respect therefore does not make her conduct uniformly generous or establish that interpretations have identical evidential support. Mel's choice to draw her own ending comes from being moved by fans' actual making, not merely buying a gift that guarantees forgiveness (006u0039–0081;007s001u0004–0033).

3. Wanted work has actual costs and needs other people

Takane sets four days because the annual new-book event is four days away; the present gathering features existing books. Mel accepts the hurdle because it may help produce something she and Momiji can accept. No global calendar follows from that local deadline. Mel explicitly names this her own wish, 姫木メルのワガママ, and releases Teacher from obligation; Teacher chooses to continue (007s001u0034–0063;s002u0012–0017).

Buying and carrying books has a physical and financial weight Mel calls the weight of happiness while denying that her general account is necessarily autobiographical. The original plan to read everything is abandoned because four days are insufficient. Reference work becomes selective while production advances. That represented adjustment is not a warrant for the analyst to omit required primary objects (007s002u0004–0022).

The deadline montage retains fatigue rather than converting effort into uncomplicated virtue. Mel dozes immediately on a chair; Teacher asks her to wake for washing and teeth, and she objects. Less than three hours of sleep and roughly thirteen continuous working hours are their estimates. Takane's excited reading of the unfinished first half genuinely responds to characters and foreshadowing, then demands completion before sleeping. She actually makes coffee; Mel actually drinks it and says it wakes her somewhat. These are local acts and claims, not validated caffeine efficacy or a safe labor standard. Her refusal to call an unfinished half complete exposes the dependence Mel inwardly recognizes on Momiji's assistance (007s002u0024–0092).

008 gives stronger endpoints: Mel asks to be left alone, falls asleep, and is narrated as having lost consciousness before Teacher puts her in bed. That supplied description is retained without diagnosis. Momiji independently calls Teacher because she too wants reconciliation. She acknowledges that the criticism could reasonably arise from an author's perspective and that she became emotional. She says nobody required this elaborate production; affection for the gesture does not require agreement with its costs. Mel overhears some, not all, of their call. The awkwardness is not fixed by Teacher pretending to handle everything: the supplied choice explicitly recognizes adult limits before suggesting a face-to-face meeting (008s001u0005–0011;s002u0013–0064).

009 begins with an important contrary act. Mel objects that Teacher's guidance produced a meeting before she is ready, refuses to go, and calls being carried away kidnapping. No legal classification is supplied, but her refusal and represented physical removal must remain alongside the successful meeting (009s002u0002–0006).

At the meeting Mel apologizes, calls Luna interesting, promises to reorder pancake tempura and apologizes again. Momiji apologizes for duplicate ordering and promises to prioritize new books. The promises are not printed fulfillment. Mel corrects even her own popularity-based justification: seeing many fans matters to her understanding, but fanless stories also deserve respect. Narration represents an awkward reconciliation gradually proceeding. This is an actual positive relationship endpoint without proof of permanent behavioral reform (009s003u0005–0035).

The manuscript is no longer necessary to obtain forgiveness. Mel nonetheless chooses to finish because she wants to create and give something to her friend; Momiji notes the oddity of asking the gift recipient to help, then actually agrees. Their renewed argument concerns characterization, page count, time and downstream printing burden. They call it debate toward a better work. Teacher remains unsure. Momiji's joy at returning to the comfortable library also matters; Mel's insistence on immediate work interrupts it. Reconciliation restores collaboration and chosen company while leaving impatience, resource conflict and exhaustion in view (009s003u0036–0070;s004u0002–0020).

D-0 supplies completed manuscript work but not necessarily printing. Mel still insists that printing remains necessary; Teacher estimates three hours left.013 depicts delivery and actual acceptance of the manuscript.015 depicts Takane actually reading it. No explicit completed print run, sale total, widespread distribution, original Luna22 publication or future event participation should be substituted for those endpoints (009s004u0021–0033;013u0007–0012;015u0024–0046).

5. Institutions try to convert this project into their own instrument

The Secretariat's medal is conditional on inserting Cherino, with a further award if she becomes protagonist. Mel refuses, proposes creating their own book or paying proper outsourcing compensation, and still personally declines. Momiji affirms knowledge's protection. The subsequent threat of force and next episode's report of repelling the Secretariat are actual local conflict, not a proven universal censorship statute or lasting liberation (010u0007–0038;011u0002–0009).

Minori values past literary assistance but demands revolutionary content and worker struggle for this book. Momiji expresses gratitude for Works Club assistance/library visits while refusing this demand. Minori then threatens struggle to correct their vision. A declared alliance is not formed simply because both use liberation language.012 says they managed the encounter without displaying its full battle mechanics. Nodoka's wish for ordinary heating, bedding, freedom from insects and hungry bears, and Shigure's proposed stove bargain are serious material preferences. Their plan to appropriate the book for Cherino is nevertheless refused; the ending prints no new stove, suspension release or physical battle for this encounter (011u0010–0035;012u0002–0016).

Yakumo later tries to claim Mel's Luna manuscript for a film about the whole adventure. She expressly disclaims acquiring copyright and unauthorized commercial publication, but envisages a long loan/possible transfer and one or two years before return. Mel repeatedly refuses. Yakumo recruits the Secretariat through school-rule/contract language. These are represented claims and coercive acts, not a finding that the contract legally permits them. Marina mistakenly associates Teacher with rule-breaking and threatens confinement; her assertion that her own reflection-room visits are comfortable does not establish Teacher's or the authors' consent (014u0010–0063).

015 begins after defeat: Yakumo withdraws this manuscript claim, yet keeps the next-manuscript demand alive. No final rescission or complete institutional reform follows. Takane distinguishes herself from her club head. Her review acknowledges plain/classic storytelling, sincerity and the possibility of better work with more time; effort alone is not a universally superior artwork claim. Her earlier response to the unfinished half and later qualified praise keep criticism and fandom together rather than removing evaluative difference (015u0001–0054).

The homeward ending preserves both warmth and objection. Momiji starts to say the gesture made her happy; Mel cuts her off with all's-well rhetoric. Momiji then insists that four days of work imposed on her and Teacher were difficult, that claimed agreement does not make every act acceptable, and that Teacher saying it was fine does not make it fine for her. The narrator is no longer worried by this quarrel, but her actual different response remains. This ending is stronger than permanent harmony: they can stay together without eliminating disagreement or the need to listen (015u0055–0079).

6. Contextual contribution and remaining limits

This event gives Red Winter's ordinary life and institutional conflict a substantive shared account. Books, food ownership, warmth, sleep, craft, fan desire, differentiated criticism and uncompleted creative work are not merely preparation for political action. Conversely, sincere affection does not justify confiscation, coerced themes, instrumental biography, forced movement or overwork. All ten episode priorities and substantive functions

E001 — CORE: material need and the publishing bargain.
Mel reports roughly three days without food, loss of hunger and weakness; Momiji reports delayed club money and a hurried, unsuccessful attempt to fund the Knowledge Liberation Front through books (s1u2–27). The repeated 'tomorrow' canteen repair and possible strike are represented uncertainty, not verified completion or a new labor event. Food is supplied before Mel's stomach pain; Takane gives water and offers a physiological explanation (u34–40), not a credentialed examination/cure. Yakumo promises to bill for the food and demands printing costs. Mel's furious offer to take things and Yakumo's acceptance expose bargaining under deprivation (u43–51).

Takane's critique identifies diluted authorial taste, little broad appeal and too little editing time; her1.5/5 is an in-world review, not our grading/model (u52–68). Yakumo attacks the assumption that quality alone attracts fans and identifies missing publicity (u70–87). Both judgments are situated, not exhaustive causal proof. Consignment is proposed under the explicit line that Mel has no choice unless she can pay now (u91–108). The9:1 split in the publisher's favor is proposed, rejected by Mel and challenged by Takane (u109–113). The subsequent contract exists, with sales-based remittance, but the final ratio is not printed (s2u2–3). Do not preserve9:1 as an executed contract term.

The supposedly perfect initial strategy sells no copies (s2u6–14). Takane interprets local familiarity with Mel's themes; Yakumo interprets Red Winter's limited spending power. Neither interpretation alone supplies a financial census. The Red Bear editor's absence after a purge, absorbed editorial staff, improved publishing finance and resulting administrative interference are reports (s2u23–30), not independently reconstructed incidents. The decision to go to Trinity combines a reading/wealth assumption with Takane's other-autonomy objection (s2u34–47). Her reluctance is already consequential.

E002 — CORE: actual enjoyment, sales rhetoric and peer circulation.
Easy entry surprises both visitors and contradicts their expected checkpoints or possible bribes (u1–18), without establishing that Trinity is universally open. A greeting student repeats a bear-training stereotype and describes efforts at exchange (u19–31); neither establishes that all Red Winter people train with bears or all Trinity people share her politics. The first reader experiences the book as overwhelming, receives227kompot, and says she likes it (u32–51). The text does not supply detailed contents that would license invented sexual acts. Yakumo markets editorial omissions as imaginative space and explains the administrative censorship/editing background (u52–72). This is a commercial theory about reader response, not proof that every omission improves every work.

The first buyer accepts three copies after a15% offer: viewing, preservation and sharing purposes are sold as 'common knowledge' (u73–92). The purchase is actual; three copies are not a genuine mandatory norm. Korean-labeled peer scenes show wanted sharing, a visit invitation and a fan's own imagined continuation (u98–113). These supply independent pleasure and creativity, not merely conversion statistics. The 'Sister' language in u108 remains locally ambiguous; it does not establish a separately narrated consensual physical act.

Nagisa's tea passage matters before the alarm: she identifies taste and fragrance, thanks the preparer, enjoys peace and wishes the teacher were there (u114–121). Pleasure and company have intrinsic weight. Her favorable assumption about whispered book discussion is then contradicted by her shocked reading (u122–136). That shock repeats at the next episode's opening and is one transition, not two incidents.

E003 — CORE: a secret commission and a librarian's contrary account.
The administrator reads at Nagisa's request, accepts instructions, but inwardly likes the book and particular subsequent developments (u1–13). Nagisa calls the book an intentional attack on Trinity's spirit and discipline (u17–27); the teacher sees an ordinary-looking manga and no particular issue. Her intention claim is unproved and explicitly challenged as a logical leap by Shimiko and a teacher option (u40–46). Ui was invited, but Shimiko arrives as substitute without a fully narrated reason (u28–32).

Shimiko inwardly knows the content, publicly denies knowing it under the atmosphere, and later admits she read to the end (u37–38,105–108). Preserve this strategic concealment rather than turning her into an unread investigator. Nagisa frames diplomacy and public atmosphere as reasons not to send the Tea Party/JTF openly, then formally and secretly commissions the teacher and library committee, allows JTF cooperation and appoints Shimiko temporary external advisor (u47–72). These are actual represented institutional decisions; they do not prove a foreign attack, unlimited legal power or a general library charter.

Mika's excitement at the teacher's approving line is followed by an inner self-correction. Several apparent Seia-style replies are printed under Mika/Nagisa labels (u78,90,92), and a Mika-like surprised line is printed as Nagisa u83. A collective exchange about overprotection is supportable; exact reassignment is not silently performed. Nagisa blocks the book, Shimiko supplies an 'apocrypha' cover story, and the adult's option criticizes the excess; Nagisa apologizes (u80–98). No Sisterhood authorization is thereby proved.

Shimiko calls the work a grey zone, neither readily recommended nor blindly suppressed, and appreciates its editing (u110–123). Her book-rights/information-value philosophy questions who licenses judgment (u124–127). Her whip-and-atonement remark is a proposed punitive position (u128–129), not a completed punishment. An anti-ban stance can coexist with coercive book protection.

E004 — HIGH: settlement, fatigue, culture theory and unread enforcement.
The publishers' lodging costs, fatigue and sales exceeding expectations are explicit (s1u2–23). Large numbers of zeroes are noticed, but no exact amount is printed. A day's settlement is transmitted to Mel/Momiji, they express surprise and thanks, and Yakumo credits the book's quality while admitting she cannot sell a hopeless book (u34–60). This contradicts a sole-marketing or sole-greed essence. Proposed food and rest are not a separately narrated meal or sleep. Literal Momiji u43/u54 and Yakumo u69 carry adjacent-actor styles; collective gratitude/settlement is firm, individual reassignment remains limited.

Yakumo explains culture as circulation rooted in money; Takane comments on inflated exchange value (u24–33). They are competing theories. The later use of Takane's 'highborn' appearance is explicitly marketing rather than100% factual representation (u73–81).

Mashiro says unapproved books should be eradicated, without having read the contents, and actually dispatches members to find sellers (s2u2–18). Her self-question at u8 is a printed actor seam. The teacher worries for both investigator and sellers. Shimiko claims book lovers cannot be bad and reasons that money alone would not require choosing books (s2u20–29). That is an interested ethical inference, not a finding that all publishers are harmless.

E005 — HIGH: readers' refuge and Koharu's ambivalent help.
Students take the sellers to an unused gym and explain the investigation, Tea Party rumors and possible seizure/exile (s1u2–11;s2u2–44). Predicted confiscation of all purchased books or profits is not completed enforcement. Readers actively shelter the publishers, and Yakumo sees suppression as an opportunity to sell more (s2u45–54). Takane agrees to the embarrassing next marketing step after explicitly asking whether it is necessary (u55–59); agreement is not unqualified enthusiasm.

Koharu meets JTF peers, learns the requested source/circulation/impact investigation, asks for samples and denies wanting them for herself; she requests more and is allowed to keep the sample (s2u60–95). Personal curiosity is a supported interpretation, but her declared wish to help should not be erased. Her desire to become an elite JTF member is future aspiration, not current membership. Mashiro's investigation stalls; the 'aura' corrupting pure classmates is her anxious speculation, corrected by the adult and by her own acknowledgment (s3u2–10), not actual paranormal attack. Shimiko obtains the continuation sample; the teacher inwardly recognizes some plot/characters (s3u11–20), still without a named, verified external source join.

E006 — CORE: genuine criticism, a false persona, original creation and books as dialogue.
Readers actually help distribute. Takane names voluntary cultural soft power and wants to visit the central/old libraries, while Yakumo says she is uninterested unless she can turn them into sales (s1u2–13). That difference matters. Yakumo says she will not force the princess routine if truly unwanted, then reminds Takane everyone already knows it; public expectation makes the choice costly (u14–25). Takane explicitly rejects the invented fallen-family youngest-daughter biography; only photography is real (u26–40). Reader interest in her explanations is genuine, but prestige founded on the false biography is not validated by that interest. She refuses the proposed criticism collection (u41–44).

A reader condemns the book as indecent, returns denying curiosity, and buys two copies after Yakumo adapts the offer to her reluctance to share (u45–69). Neither her opening refusal nor eventual purchase should swallow the other. Takane's love/body/contradiction criticism is substantive speech and received by appreciative listeners; her inward stomach pain remains (u70–82). It does not narrate the fictional contents as real acts.

A two-line request creates an opportunity for Mel. She initially objects to commission burdens and revisions; Yakumo offers freedom in the unspecified parts and invokes her wanted original creation, and Mel explicitly accepts and begins (u85–117). This is not a completed delivered commission or100% original work. Literal Mel u107 carries the publisher's persuasion: retain the actor seam. Creative desire remains intrinsic even within monetization.

At the café, Koharu admits giving Shimiko the sample because fans would be sad to lose something they love (s2u17–24). This is an independent ethical position, not reducible to hidden desire. She denies interest and accepts a future full-series inspection framed as elite work (u25–31), not completed reading. Shimiko's 'time machine' is explicitly a metaphor: books create room to think and answer past writers in one's own terms (u33–56). It is her media philosophy, not an objective rule that films/games permit no reflection. The teacher's 'there are no bad people' option is a represented overbroad affirmation, not our universal ledger claim.

The teacher asks Koharu to spend time with her former JTF peers when activity increases; she says she is not currently JTF and agrees after reassurance (u62–73). Her help is requested and given; no universal reception guarantee follows. Nagisa intends to encourage Mashiro and lessen the burden; Mashiro hears renewed institutional concern and vows success (u74–82). This miscommunication is more precise than a deliberate Nagisa threat.

E007 — CORE: pressure, withdrawn help, wanted shelter and personal distance.
Mashiro turns that misread concern into a test of JTF existence/value and expands all human resources immediately, acknowledging the unreasonable request as members ask her to wait (u1–21). The publishers actually have no sales and no venue that day (u22–25). A reader warns of collection of all nontextbooks; this is a student report, not independently verified full implementation (u30–38). She says she can no longer help. Takane thanks her, values the memories already made and questions whether always going to the end is wise (u39–55). This legitimate limit should not become treachery or failed affection.

They find the old library. Ui asks for silence, recognizes care for books, corrects the exaggerated total-library rumor and likes their comic (u60–93). Her assertion that a building disappeared as punishment for overdue books is an attributed confirmation (u83–86), not our new whole prior-incident reading. She infers Tea Party involvement, offers temporary shelter and says long stays are unwelcome (u94–105). She requires three metres of distance, then clarifies that it is her personal issue rather than strictly a rule (u106–115). Help includes recipient conditions. No dark-loving essence replaces her actual preferences. Takane calls the teacher while wishing she could instead tell a praiseworthy story (u124–131); wanted approval and difficult honesty coexist.

E008 — CORE: the market-ring argument challenged by attachment and false advertising.
Ui welcomes the teacher specifically, feels four people are too many, and receives a quietness promise (u1–6). Yakumo first gives money as motive, then develops the market-ring and money-soil argument: unheard work deserves a chance to succeed, learn, change direction or fail (u11–56). It is a meaningful theory, not a fact that all cultural worth equals price. The teacher questions the young person's fatalism and asks why, if money alone matters, not pursue another industry (u47,57–61). Takane explicitly says she and the publisher work there because they like it (u62–70), then hints that the lost-talent/champion story concerns Yakumo herself (u71–75). The hint permits an interpretation, not an established full creative biography.

The adult calls the princess lie dangerous. Takane insists it went too far and remains embarrassing. Yakumo agrees to end this episode of activity (u78–83). A warning of approaching JTF follows (u84), so this agreement is not yet a secured resolution or an actual return home.

E009 — CORE: access, protective violence and a procedural local resolution.
Koharu has actually accompanied peers and warns the teacher; Shimiko advises her to avoid the conflict, but she decides to go because it is right (u1–26). The source of the JTF tip is not identified, so do not brand Koharu a confirmed informant. Mashiro proposes a complete library inventory and possible removal; her assertion that innocence leaves no reason to refuse is immediately contested (u30–52). Ui threatens wrists, interprets the inquiry as a Tea Party takeover, and demands that they defeat her first; JTF members also threaten force (u53–75). The alleged takeover intention is unverified, and neither caretaker nor investigator controls an ethically pure stance.

The teacher/Shimiko stop the impending clash (u76–80). Ui accuses Shimiko of betrayal and cries during Shimiko's rebuke; Shimiko refers to prior hospitalizations and says not to shoot people (u87–94). These do not establish a new number of injured people or a fully narrated fresh battle/punishment method. Takane comes out to apologize, explicitly declining internal school conflict as a result she wanted; Yakumo apologizes too (u101–123). Their story is heard. Yakumo says that seeing happy readers developed her cultural motive; it was not the initial grand purpose (u132–140). This evolving statement should not erase both profit and pleasure.

The teacher proposes library permission. Shimiko says library responsibility makes approval possible and expects some adjustment; Ui personally thinks adjustment unnecessary, approves, and delegates others' judgments (u141–165). Mashiro accepts process as a way to build justice and plans to report; the adult volunteers to accompany (u149–172). This is a genuine local resolution, not proof of a universal policy or already tested international agreement. Literal Koharu u112, Takane u117, Shimiko u128 and Ui u167 have adjacent-actor styles: retain those seams. The now locally approved book is finally read by Mashiro and interested members; Koharu's shock culminates in the familiar ban/death cry (u174–181). That is no actual sentence and does not cancel her prior defense of readers.

E010 — CORE: qualified exchange, taste, oversight and unfinished desires.
Nagisa presents a cultural-exchange proposal, with the teacher as guarantor and library judgment, expresses Tea Party assent and asks that future circulation wait for consultation (u1–4). The proposal details are represented speech, not a separately received treaty document. Cherino delegates this case to Schale and leaves for a nap (u5–14). The teacher is surprised. Nagisa's liability/emotional-risk interpretation calls this cunning diplomacy (u15–23); it is her inward construction, not verified secret intent. The nap should not become a covert signal without evidence.

Nagisa welcomes the publishers and future recommendations (u28–32). Mika says she read and liked the book, compares its protagonist to the teacher and proposes a pink-haired, lively heroine with jumbo-parfait/fashion preferences and no more roll cake (u33–54). These preferences are given within a fictional proposal, not a new private-family source completion. Yakumo offers a costly one-person remake; an unprinted amount surprises her, and she says half would suffice. Nagisa stops it (u56–75). No price, payment, completed commission or delivered personal book exists here. Mika u55 carries Yakumo-style speech.

Mashiro reports more library visits/new interests and explicitly wants a continuation because she very much likes the book (u76–89). This is real taste beyond initial institutional certainty; the story itself is not finished. The request for a princess criticism collection persists, Takane only agrees to consider, and then objects that marketing is no excuse (u90–100). Her false biography's consequences remain unresolved. The teacher promises to keep watching Yakumo and states that going too far could exceed the adult's ability to take responsibility; Yakumo acknowledges this but reframes continued attention positively (u101–111). This is a qualified oversight relationship, not complete rehabilitation or unlimited guarantorship. She admits she did not ask for help initially because she expected a scolding (u114–119). The adult ends with a day's work completed, not the whole arc.

Comparative judgment and rival readings

The event advances the Trinity V003/V006 questions about assumed intent, protection and public authority at an ordinary reading/cultural-work scope. Nagisa's claim of an internal attack is explicitly contested. It still creates a real secret commission, and its personnel misunderstand each other. Mashiro's sincere effort becomes an existence test that burdens colleagues and affects ordinary readers. Ui's care for books justifies meaningful refusal of indiscriminate removal, but her violent rhetoric and prior-punishment claim remain contrary evidence. The procedural answer changes local status; it does not retrospectively make every enforcement step justified.

The public peer world is differentiated. Some students greet outsiders while repeating stereotypes; some shelter publishers, others return after condemning the work, one withdraws help with legitimate limits, and Koharu protects the fans while continuing to disclaim personal interest. Shimiko preserves room for interpretation, enjoys precise editing, hides reading under pressure and admits it later. Takane is critic, reluctant performer, would-be library visitor and ethical interrupter. Yakumo negotiates aggressively, manipulates persona, praises the book, opens a useful market and admits changing motives. A single book-loving benevolent essence would miss all of these differences.

A favorable interpretation treats circulation as giving neglected creative work and readers a chance to meet. It has actual support: first purchase, peer sharing/fan creation, settlements, Mel's original-work aspiration, Ui's reading approval and Mashiro's new taste. A contrary interpretation sees monetization and institutional control both converting others' preferences into instruments. That has support too: starvation leverage, the rejected9:1 demand, prestige deception, public pressure on Takane, covert investigation, unread condemnation and possible removal. The ending offers a locally workable procedure and oversight limits; it does not erase those mechanisms or establish stable future profit.

Pleasure is not only compensation after conflict. Nagisa's tea, Takane's photography/library curiosity and criticism, readers' sharing and making, Mel's wanted creation, Shimiko's thought-space, Ui's quiet conditions, Mashiro's genuine continuation wish and Mika's fictional self-like heroine desire all matter intrinsically. None requires an invented performed act, credential, delivered gift or completed future commission.

Japanese, source modes and chronology

非公認/公認 indicate the local procedural distinction enacted in dialogue; they are not synonyms for intrinsic harmfulness/harmlessness. 検閲 versus 編集 is deliberately contested and used as a marketing device. 健全, 芸術, グレーゾーン and the displayed ban/death language are positions and comic rhetoric, not independent legal classifications. タカネ姫/冬の国の公女様 is an invented persona, explicitly contradicted by Takane; no noble lineage should be admitted from the readers' story. 本 as children/persons and タイムマシン are caretaker/metaphoric usage, explicitly qualified in E006. Yakumo's market ring and money-soil remain argument rather than natural law.

The canonical spoken/inward/italic and Korean actor labels are preserved. Seia-like lines under other labels make a collective overprotection exchange legible but prevent silently assigned individual quotations. Unknown or mistaken actor resolution does not prevent interpreting reliable adjacent action, but it bounds precision. No audiovisual performance was received. Teacher choices show represented praise, criticism, reassurance, procedure and responsibility limits; they do not prove all unselected alternatives occurred.

The first day, following day, several days of search and eventual exchange proposal establish local sequence. The foodless three days, last week's manuscript and anticipated repair/possible strike are reported/local markers, not a global Kivotos date. Red Bear history and Ui's prior punishment remain attributed. E002/E003 repeat one shocked transition. This event cannot by itself date the whole V003/V006 public arc or every private family.

complete_actual_selected_passages.text:
Takane does not reduce to either a harsh critic or a secretly genuine princess. The complete selection makes criticism a desired craft of revealing hidden value, while cooking a simple inexpensive dish, watching hockey and photographing landscapes have their own value. Her critical pose is fallible: strong subjective fandom can become gatekeeping in the public event, a hockey rule explanation fails against the broadcast's escalating violence, and she dislikes the improvised work she was pressed to make. She nevertheless appreciates an actual photo and wants the evening private. Creative role and everyday identity are explicitly distinguished, not biographically merged.

Yakumo's plans are intrinsically enjoyable even when rejected. She wants publication to remain viable, readers to enjoy content, warm rest and rail/bento pleasure; her strategic instrumental use of users' wants coexists with stated spending caps and a concrete refusal to overbuy/waste food. Operating rights are explicitly distinguished from ownership. Her attempts to enlist SCHALE's prestige are refused repeatedly, while everyday work still finishes. The snow-photo thread includes a positive reported sales result, then a rejected new interview. No blanket rule of commercial purity, harmlessness, universal success or malign business essence adequately describes these endings.

The paired argument makes boundaries consequential in both directions. Takane acknowledges an adult's concealed-book privacy yet presses again, limits her own sensitive answers and gives an invitation with a refusal off-ramp. The adult then presses a creative performance and imposed princess framing; her later displeasure is printed alongside beauty and gratitude. Yakumo is refused political favors and unlimited company, refuses extra timetable labor, objects to unilateral cold-photo exposure and asks reciprocity. Public Mel's refusal of manuscript appropriation and Yakumo's own attempted event-gift exit remain separate recipient boundaries. A pleasurable outcome does not cancel prior pressure, refusal or outstanding institutional claims.

## 3. Takane: four full private pairs

### 3.1 評論の対象 — BA:bond:10131:002 and wholeMM101310010

First SCHALE visiting and warmth are printed at scene001:u0001–0003. Takane wants reciprocal knowledge (u0006–0015). She first says people are formally outside critique's target (u0011), then proposes the analogy of analyzing/composing information to reveal value (u0012–0015). This is her positive relational theory, not certified permission to inspect any person.

A book found under Teacher's desk (u0018) attracts her intended reading (u0019); Teacher explicitly refuses at choice006, strongly repeats the boundary in the dialogue she answers, and uses a hyperbolic “kill me first” formulation at choice007. No killing or actual reading/content of the book is narrated. Takane recognizes privacy (u0023) yet presses tolerance/permission again (u0024–0025). The adult's concealed object remains unknown, not an invented genre or moral accusation.

She argues that classification creates meaning (u0031–0033), gives this month's cultural critique collection (u0034–0035), and disparages Mel's pages22–24 (u0036–0037). Those pages are not personally read here; her statement is not an independent literary judgment. She reports shared authorship and tries to fill her pages, but sometimes finds no work worth criticizing (u0038–0039). Analog-only unsustainability, broad commercial diversification and regret at straying from publishing (u0040–0043) are her institutional claims, not an industry audit. Her wish to leave valuable criticism as professional duty (u0045–0046) is actually expressed.

The claim that Teacher values student gifts and conceals something (u0051–0052) arises from this encounter; it is not a complete adult psyche. Her own answer availability is limited for sensitive subjects (u0053–0056), despite agreeing to questions. Hockey hobby surprises Teacher (u0063); she overestimates adult knowledge at u0066, then corrects her expectation (u0067–0069). The invitation to watch and explain/“critique” hockey (u0071–0073) is prospective at the BOND ending.

Whole MM101310010 messages101310010–101310210 includes formal duty greeting, the adult's wish for easier communication and her concern about burden. W15 launch080 is not EOF. Tail090–210 requests a semifinal date, apologizes for not first checking availability at130–140, receives adult reassurance150 and willingness to adjust after receiving the schedule190. It is not a globally dated appointment. Later E003/MM150 provides local continuity at its own words.

### 3.2 アイスホッケー — BA:bond:10131:003 and wholeMM101310150

The workshop lacks screening equipment; they actually move to a prepared screening room (scene001:u0002–0007). Takane reports the club's broad cultural-business control (u0009–0012), defends local procedure and denies unjust personal gain (u0013–0014). These claims do not establish a monopoly or financial innocence, while the useful screening resource actually exists.

Hockey broadcasting begins at u0019. Her six-player/three20-minute-period/goaltender explanation (u0021–0024) is source-located fictional speech, not external sports regulation. Body checking is treated as acceptable (u0026), and she urges the knocked-down player to rise rather than delay (u0027); pleasure and bodily aggression are both retained. Stick-hit penalty and bribery suspicion (u0029–0030) remain her judgment/suspicion. The adult's choice007 alternatives observe repeated checks/cracked glass; her predicted interruption/penalty (u0031–0032) is contradicted by announced resumption (u0033). Her referee threat (u0034) is not a personally enacted attack.

The adult inward observation shows audience incursion/flag burning (u0041). Crowd accusations blame the bureau for cold, pudding quality, workweek and defeat (u0048–0054); their anger is actual speech, causation unverified. The bureau announces coup/martial law/safety (u0059–0062), while an open microphone exposes escape-duration bets (u0063–0069). This is an institutional contradiction at the broadcast scale, not an adjudicated government change.

Takane concedes that the day is dangerous and proposes classic-match highlights (u0072–0073); **they actually watch the compilation at u0074**. Present disruption does not erase desired sports company or make her abandon fandom. No calm public resolution, penalty repair, payment audit or safe sports policy is printed. Whole MM101310150 messages101310220–101310270 confirms the local viewing appointment and adult enjoyment/waiting; its launch270 is also EOF, without invented afterword.

### 3.3 もやし祭り — BA:bond:10131:005 and wholeMM101310190

The actual location is the Third Public Cafeteria kitchen. Simple, inexpensive beansprouts are a desired ingredient (scene001:u0003–0006), with quick cooking and texture difficulty giving her a concrete craft account. She invents the festival name (u0007) and reports a biweekly Wednesday routine (u0008), not a calendar for every source. Nutrition and morning-illness claims (u0004/u0016/u0026) are in-fiction formulations, not verified dietary/clinical advice.

Her livelihood/controversy account of criticism (u0018–0019) becomes heated, followed by apology (u0020–0021). It does not negate the professional respect for hidden value elsewhere. Pork/beansprout oyster stir-fry is actually ready (u0023–0028). Rice, side-dish, bread and rye serving possibilities (u0029–0030) are alternatives/offers, not all consumed combinations. Teacher's inward taste/warmth response (u0031) and the **shared heart-warming table at u0034** are actual local pleasure. Refills are offered at u0033, not measured consumption.

Whole MM101310190 messages101310280–101310390 explicitly thanks the earlier hockey company and apologizes for the disturbance280/300–310. Teacher says it was enjoyable320; she offers apology lunch340–350. This is a positive specific repair of a disappointing outing at the dyadic scale, not restitution for the audience's violence or institutional wrongdoing. Launch390 is EOF.

### 3.4 夜空に佇む姫君 — BA:bond:10131:006 and wholeMM101310280

Landscape photography is her preference (scene001:u0005). She theorizes criticism as developing/fixing impressions and gaining a measure of objectivity through others' reading (u0008–0018), while photographs begin from objects yet show the photographer's subjectivity. These are her thoughtful aesthetic distinctions, not a universal validated method. The creation-wish question (u0021) prompts hesitation (u0022–0024); it does not establish concealed autobiography. An aurora is actually observed at u0025, beyond the app forecast.

She doubts critique's smallness before nature (u0027–0028), values human-made beauty (u0029–0033), and resists the adult's photo/concept request: unqualified creation can slight creators and hurt others (u0035–0042). The private audience/secrecy proposal (u0043–0044), her request for a keyword (u0047) and acceptance of the supplied role (u0049) establish the actual creative framework. The adult's additive-beauty argument is mocked by her chocolate-mint/takoyaki analogy (u0037–0038), not endorsed as a sound aesthetic formula.

**Three sisters, frail childhood, Shvibzik, Maria, unwanted cold baths, fallen household and dispersed/lost family in u0051–0058/u0065–0066 belong to the agreed exiled-princess fiction. They are not Takane's personal biography, diagnoses or family registry.** Timed log tagged 타카네 at u0059–0076 is written creative speech. “Partner”u0072 and Teacher's inward recognitionu0073 are explicitly qualified by “now that is the setting”u0075. No permanent romantic/exclusive partner is registered.

Afterward she says she is not a princess, that the story is over and she remains Miyoshi Takane (u0078). She sharply dislikes the improvised work (u0079–0080), and points to Teacher having asked her to do it (u0081). Her annoyance stays despite the **actual photo's beauty/appreciation at u0084–0085**. She asks that the photo and evening not be shared (u0087–0090); future confidentiality compliance is unprinted.

Whole MM101310280 messages101310400–101310620 has an explicit invitation off-ramp510–520. Adult530/540 are alternatives—responding to her request versus a “legal”escape from overtime—not both one executed history. Both actual schedule launch witnesses580 and620 bind the same E006; neither supplies a second selected thread. Gratitude/embarrassment550–580 and deadline-walk sympathy590–610 are preserved. The final waiting620 remains an invitation endpoint at this thread's scope.

## 4. Yakumo: four full private pairs

The remote communication-line project and the bureau contract are stated by Yakumo (scene001:u0007–0013). Workers actually arrive and ask about pudding/Mors rewards (u0016–0018); her trust/payment promise (u0019–0020) is not a completed wage record. The adult initially expects minimizing worker compensation (choice005); her reply and infrastructure rationale complicate that preconception.

Her inadequate-budget and life-line arguments (u0029–0034) distinguish cheap useful infrastructure from extracting immediate user profit. **Operation rights, not ownership**, are explicitly specified twice (u0035–0036). These are her planned bargain and commercial reasoning, not a validated public privatization settlement. Wired dorm access is positively reported by actual recipients (u0039–0040), with prior expensive/unstable wireless conditions as their reports.

Reading pleasure and marketing are both real. Students actually finish free web fiction and report having paid/read onward (u0054–0058); demand exceeds Yakumo's expectation (u0059–0060).
